goal: Extract the enforced-attributes responsibility from Safelist into a dedicated SafelistEnforcedAttributes class to improve modularization and isolate enforcement data & operations.

expected_impact.rationale: This extraction isolates the enforced-attribute data structures and related helper operations into a dedicated class. Although Safelist already exposes public APIs that delegate to this manager, extracting the full enforcement responsibility centralizes logic, reduces Safelist's implementation volume, and improves cohesion. Public API count on Safelist remains unchanged (delegation preserved), but Safelist's implementation LOC and internal complexity are reduced.

ops.details: Create a new package-class SafelistEnforcedAttributes that encapsulates the enforced-attributes map and provides the following methods used by Safelist: getInternalMap(), addEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute, String value), removeEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute), getEnforcedValue(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key), hasEnforcedAttribute(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key), and getEnforcedAttributes(String tagName) returning org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes. The new class uses the existing Safelist inner typed classes (Safelist.TagName, Safelist.AttributeKey, Safelist.AttributeValue) for keys/values and stores data in a Map<Safelist.TagName, Map<Safelist.AttributeKey, Safelist.AttributeValue>>. No public Safelist APIs are removed; Safelist continues to hold a private final SafelistEnforcedAttributes enforcedAttributesManager field and to delegate to it. The extraction centralizes enforcement logic and data into its own file in the same package.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.

extraction_notes: The new class will be package-visible in org.jsoup.safety and reference Safelist.TagName, Safelist.AttributeKey, and Safelist.AttributeValue (static inner classes of Safelist). Because Safelist already instantiates and calls the listed methods on enforcedAttributesManager, adding this class is backward-compatible and compiles without further API changes. This reduces Safelist implementation LOC and groups enforcement responsibilities into a cohesive unit.
